prompt: How many solutions does $\sin(2\theta) = \cos\theta$ have on $0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ$?
hint: Replace $\sin(2\theta)$ with $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ so both sides use the same angle.

hints.text: Replace $\sin(2\theta)$ with $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ so both sides use the same angle.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up by counting solutions of $\sin\theta\cos\theta = 0$: the $\cos\theta = 0$ branch gives $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$, the $\sin\theta = 0$ branch gives $0^\circ$ and $180^\circ$, so four in all. Factor, then count every branch.
Move everything to one side and FACTOR: $2\sin\theta\cos\theta - \cos\theta = 0$, so $\cos\theta(2\sin\theta - 1) = 0$.
$\cos\theta = 0$ gives $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$; $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ gives $30^\circ$ and $150^\circ$. That is $4$ solutions.

explanation: Use the double-angle formula to write the equation as $2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \cos\theta$.
Bring everything to one side and factor out the common $\cos\theta$: $\cos\theta(2\sin\theta - 1) = 0$.
Set each factor to zero. $\cos\theta = 0$ gives $\theta = 90^\circ, 270^\circ$; $2\sin\theta - 1 = 0$ gives $\theta = 30^\circ, 150^\circ$.
All four values lie in the interval, so there are $4$ solutions.

alternativeExplanations.title: See it as two graphs crossing
steps: Sketch $y = \sin(2\theta)$, which completes two full cycles across $0^\circ$ to $360^\circ$, and $y = \cos\theta$, which completes one.
A faster wave crossing a slower one over the same window meets it several times.
Counting the crossings gives $4$, matching the algebra.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap is dividing both sides by $\cos\theta$ to get $2\sin\theta = 1$, which leaves only $30^\circ$ and $150^\circ$ — an answer of $2$.
Dividing by $\cos\theta$ silently assumes $\cos\theta \ne 0$, and it throws away the two solutions where $\cos\theta$ IS zero, namely $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$.
The rule: never divide an equation by an expression containing the variable. Factor instead, and set every factor to zero. The answer is $4$.
